title: Optimize Patch Manager: API for safe rollbacks, webhook ACKs, and patch staging
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Optimize recommendations (batching/caching/quantization hints) need an API-driven path to stage configuration patches, verify safe application, and rollback automatically when regressions or failures occur. Current operability is manual: Solutions are applied via console or ad-hoc scripts which causes drift, broken rollouts, and lost auditability.

Goal: Build a Patch Manager API that supports: staged patch creation, idempotent apply semantics with dedup tokens, webhook-driven lifecycle events (proposed, applied, ack, failed, rolled_back), and a rollback orchestration endpoint. The API surface must enable SDK clients and webhooks to integrate with Optimize automation while preserving audit logs, RBAC checks, and safe revert behavior.

Constraints and non-goals: This work focuses on control-plane APIs and orchestration; it does not change serving runtime batching logic or introduce new kernel-level changes. We will rely on existing audit log storage and Dedicated RBAC primitives. Live traffic can use the existing rollout/fallback mechanisms but must be able to be triggered by the new patch manager endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: Clients can create a patch resource with a unique client_provided_dedup_token and get 201 with patch_id
Patch apply operation is idempotent: repeated apply requests with same dedup token are no-ops and return the same result/status
Webhook events emitted for all lifecycle transitions (created, staged, applied, acked, failed, rolled_back) and retries are safe (idempotent delivery)
A rollback endpoint accepts patch_id and returns a deterministic rollback task with progress events; rollback can be observed via the same webhook channel
API surface validated by SDK integration tests (JS/Python) and e2e test that simulates a regression and confirms automatic rollback
Audit logs include who initiated the patch, the dedup token, diff metadata, and the final resolution (applied/rolled_back)
implementation_notes: Design REST resources: POST /v1/patches, GET /v1/patches/{id}, POST /v1/patches/{id}/apply, POST /v1/patches/{id}/rollback
API idempotency: require header X-Dedup-Token or body field client_provided_dedup_token; store dedup mapping in control-plane DB with TTL matching retention policy
Webhook design: support subscription filter by project/model and include delivery_ack_id; delivery retries exponential backoff and Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) per project
State machine: patch states {created, staged, applying, applied, failed, rolling_back, rolled_back}; transitions must be append-only events persisted to event journal for auditability
RBAC: validate caller scope for create/apply/rollback; incorporate feature-flag to restrict auto-rollback to admin or ops roles for initial rollout
Testing: unit tests for dedup behavior, contract tests for webhooks, and integration harness that runs against staging with a sample recommendation set

2026-03-04 - Rafael Ortega: Initial API contract uploaded: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPT/Patch+Manager+API+-+Contract. Key decision: use explicit rollback endpoint rather than reverse-diff apply to ensure deterministic undo behavior.
2026-03-06 - Design review (Lina Gomez): UX feedback — add a nullable 'preview' flag to POST /patches to compute estimated token/cost delta without staging the patch. Raf to add to spec.
2026-03-08 - Security (Anita Rao): Requested KMS key audit for all patches affecting private deployments; added requirement to include kms_key_id in patch metadata for private customers.

2026-03-09 - Rafael Ortega: Implemented server skeleton and dedup mapping (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/pull/2287). Implement notes in repo README. Unit tests for dedup token added.

2026-03-11 - QA (Jordan Lee): Reported flaky webhook delivery in local harness when delivery_ack_id is present. Suspect race in in-memory DLQ simulation. Rafael investigating; plan to add persistent DLQ backing store for staging tests.

2026-03-12 - Maya Chen: Updated rollout plan: feature-flag gated, enable for internal orgs and 2 pilot customers, 1-week observation window, metrics to watch: failed_applies/sec, rollback_rate, mean_time_to_recover. Owner: Rafael (engineering), Ezra (PM).
